title: Tampa Bay rallies for 12th-inning walk-off to beat Milwaukee in World Series Game 4
text:
Tampa Bay rallies for 12th-inning walk-off to beat Milwaukee in World Series Game 4 - CHOSUNBIZ 
 2026년 10월 28일(수) Industry Finance Real Estate IT Retail Science Policy Society International Entertainment Culture Sports English Sports Tampa Bay rallies for 12th-inning walk-off to beat Milwaukee in World Series Game 4 
 입력 2026.10.28. 13:40 조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 A 12th-inning miracle happened for Tampa Bay. 
 The Tampa Bay Rays won a 4-3 walk-off victory in the 12th inning of Game 4 of the 2026 World Series (best-of-seven) against the Milwaukee Brewers on the 28th (Korea time) at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Florida.
 Having been on the brink after losing the first three games of the series, Tampa Bay finally notched its first win in Game 4 and was resurrected. Meanwhile, Milwaukee's bid for its first championship was pushed to Game 5. The eight-game winning streak that began in Game 4 of the National League Division Series was also halted.
 The home team Tampa Bay set a starting lineup against Milwaukee starter Dustin May of Yandy Díaz (designated hitter), Jonathan Aranda (first base), Junior Caminero (third base), Liam Hicks (catcher), Jonny DeLuca (center field), Chandler Simpson (left field), Ryan Vilade (right field), Richy Palacios (second base) and Curtis Taylor (shortstop).
 Milwaukee, playing on the road, submitted an order against Tampa Bay starter Griffin Jax of Jackson Chourio (left field), Jake Bauers (first base), Christian Yelich (designated hitter), William Contreras (catcher), Brice Turang (second base), Sal Frelick (right field), Cooper Pratt (shortstop), Garrett Mitchell (center field) and David Hamilton (third base).
 Milwaukee had the first scoring opportunity. In the top of the first with two outs, Yelich drew a walk and attempted to steal second, but a throwing error by catcher Hicks allowed him to get past second and reach third. Contreras also drew a walk to create a two-out, bases-loaded chance, but Turang ended the inning with a grounder to shortstop.
 Tampa Bay broke the 0-0 tie. In the bottom of the second, leadoff hitter Hicks opened the scoring with a single to center, DeLuca reached on a fielder's choice, and Simpson drove a 1-run double deep to right. Even with one out, first-base runner DeLuca used his speed to go past second and third and touch home. However, the continued one-out, runner-at-second chance ended when the next batters failed to deliver.
 Milwaukee countered in the top of the fourth. It mirrored Tampa Bay's earlier scoring. After two outs, Frelick singled to right and Pratt followed with a 1-run double to deep left to tie the game. Like DeLuca in the second, first-base runner Frelick gritted his teeth and sprinted home to score the tying run. Pratt then advanced to third on a wild pitch, and Mitchell struck out swinging to end the threat.
 Tampa Bay did not stay quiet. In the bottom of the fourth, leadoff hitter Caminero's single to left forced May out of the game. Hicks then advanced on a grounder to move Caminero to second, and on DeLuca's infield grounder, third baseman Hamilton's throw to first sailed wide, allowing runner Caminero to go past third and score. Tampa Bay led 2-1.
 Milwaukee tied it again in the top of the fifth on a solo home run by leadoff hitter Hamilton. Hamilton turned on Jax's third pitch, a 93.4-mile (150km) four-seam fastball that came high and inside on an 0-2 count, and drove it 391 feet (119m) to center-right to tie the game.
 Milwaukee lamented a missed opportunity in the top of the ninth. After one out, Pratt singled to left and Mitchell then hit a big swing that headed for the left-field warning track, but misfortune struck when left fielder Simpson made a jumping catch at the wall to rob the hit.
 The teams remained deadlocked after nine innings. Milwaukee took the lead first in the top of the 12th. Leadoff hitter Pratt faced reliever Ian Seymour and hit a dramatic solo home run. On a 2-2 count, he turned on the fifth pitch, an 83.7-mile (134km) sweeper that came inside, and sent it 396 feet (120m) to left-center for a homer.
 Tampa Bay did not back down. In the bottom of the 12th, leadoff hitter Caminero reached on a first-base throwing error by third baseman Joey Votto. Hicks followed with a hit to the left-center and set the table with no outs and runners at first and third, and DeLuca delivered a run-scoring single to center to tie the game.
 Tampa Bay, aided by Simpson's single to center with the bases loaded and no outs, rode pinch-hitter Ben Williamson's walk-off go-ahead RBI single to stage a dramatic comeback. After the opponent's error, they showed resilience by stringing together four consecutive hits.
